I. The outbreak of the revolt at Meerut
II. The annexation of Awadh
III. Thomas Jones Barker's painting 'Relief of Lucknow'
IV. The imposition of the subsidiary alliance on Awadh
items.answer: IV, II, I, III
items.markingKey: (a) The imposition of the subsidiary alliance on Awadh (1801); The annexation of Awadh (1856); The outbreak of the revolt at Meerut (1857); Thomas Jones Barker's painting 'Relief of Lucknow' (1859).

items.stem: "The rebels approached Bahadur Shah Zafar." Examine this statement with reference to the pattern of the Revolt of 1857.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The Mughal emperor was a powerful symbol of legitimacy across north India.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the Mughal emperor was a powerful symbol of legitimacy across north India.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about what the rebels wanted in 1857 is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The rebels supported the British revenue system."
items.answer: They opposed high revenue demands and the dispossession of landholders.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (They opposed high revenue demands and the dispossession of landholders.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about repression and images of the Revolt of 1857:
I. The British passed a series of Acts in May and June 1857 placing north India under martial law.
II. Pictures and cartoons formed public opinion about the revolt in Britain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about what the rebels wanted in 1857:
I. The proclamations often referred to the Mughal empire and its tradition of coexistence of different communities.
II. The British attempt to portray the revolt as Hindu-Muslim conflict found little support during the revolt.
III. Rebel proclamations appealed only to Muslims.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: They appealed to all sections irrespective of caste and creed.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on Awadh in revolt and answer the questions that follow.
"The subsidiary alliance was imposed on Awadh in 1801, and the Nawab had to disband his army. The Summary Settlement of 1856 dispossessed taluqdars of their estates and forts. Taluqdars and peasants together fought against the British in Awadh, making it one of the main centres of the revolt."
(i) Who annexed Awadh on the grounds of misgovernment? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Summary Settlement' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Sepoys from Awadh were deeply affected by the annexation. (2)
items.answer: (i) Lord Dalhousie (ii) The British revenue settlement of 1856 in Awadh that removed taluqdars wherever possible and settled with the actual owners of land. (iii) They came from Awadh's villages and their families suffered from high revenue demands and the loss of the Nawab.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Lord Dalhousie (ii) The British revenue settlement of 1856 in Awadh that removed taluqdars wherever possible and settled with the actual owners of land. (iii) They came from Awadh's villages and their families suffered from high revenue demands and the loss of the Nawab.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the pattern of the Revolt of 1857:
I. A prophecy that British rule would end on the centenary of the battle of Plassey, 23 June 1857, also circulated.
II. The rebels in Delhi proclaimed Nana Sahib as the emperor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: They proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader.

items.stem: In the study of Awadh in revolt, the term 'annexation of Awadh' refers to:
items.answer: The British takeover of Awadh in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment
items.markingKey: (b) 'annexation of Awadh' means the British takeover of Awadh in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment.
options: Military rule declared by the British in north India in 1857 under which rebels could be tried and punished by military officers
The British takeover of Awadh in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment
Cartridges of the new Enfield rifle, rumoured to be coated with the fat of cows and pigs
A rebel proclamation of 25 August 1857 that listed the grievances of zamindars, merchants, government servants, artisans and religious leaders

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Nationalist imagery made heroes of leaders like Rani Lakshmibai.
Reason (R): British paintings showed the rebels as heroes.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: British paintings showed British soldiers as heroes and rebels as savage.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about what the rebels wanted in 1857 is NOT correct?
items.answer: Rebel proclamations appealed only to Muslims.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. They appealed to all sections irrespective of caste and creed.
options: Rebel proclamations appealed only to Muslims.
The rebels wanted to restore the pre-British world of the eighteenth century.
The British attempt to portray the revolt as Hindu-Muslim conflict found little support during the revolt.
In Delhi, Lucknow and Kanpur the rebels tried to set up structures of administration based on the Mughal model.

items.stem: Explain the role of rumours and prophecies in the Revolt of 1857.
items.answer: Greased cartridges with fat of cows and pigs; bone dust in atta; prophecy that British rule would end on Plassey centenary (23 June 1857); chapatis circulated; rumours spread because they fed existing fears about British reforms, missionaries and annexations.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Greased cartridges with fat of cows and pigs; bone dust in atta; prophecy that British rule would end on Plassey centenary (23 June 1857); chapatis circulated; rumours spread because they fed existing fears about British reforms, missionaries and annexations.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on what the rebels wanted in 1857 and answer the questions that follow.
"Rebel proclamations repeatedly appealed to all sections of the population, irrespective of caste and creed. The rebels wanted to restore the pre-British world of the eighteenth century. The British attempt to portray the revolt as Hindu-Muslim conflict found little support during the revolt."
(i) Rebel proclamations in 1857 appealed to people to join: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'rebel proclamations' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The rebel proclamations stressed Hindu-Muslim unity. (2)
items.answer: (i) irrespective of their caste and creed (ii) Announcements issued by rebel leaders appealing to all sections of the population to join the fight against the British. (iii) The rebels wanted all communities to unite against the British, recalling the coexistence of the Mughal period.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) irrespective of their caste and creed (ii) Announcements issued by rebel leaders appealing to all sections of the population to join the fight against the British. (iii) The rebels wanted all communities to unite against the British, recalling the coexistence of the Mughal period.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: Shah Mal – Barout pargana
items.markingKey: (a) Shah Mal – Barout pargana. Begum Hazrat Mahal – Lucknow; Rani Lakshmibai – Jhansi; Nana Sahib – Kanpur are the correct pairs for the others.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about Awadh in revolt:
I. The Summary Settlement strengthened the taluqdars of Awadh.
II. Awadh was annexed in 1801.
III. The annexation of Awadh and the removal of Wajid Ali Shah caused widespread grief and anger among people.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is incorrect: It dispossessed them of their land and forts. II is incorrect: The subsidiary alliance was imposed in 1801; Awadh was annexed in 1856. III is correct.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? A painting by Thomas Jones Barker (1859) celebrating the British commanders who rescued the besieged British garrison at Lucknow.
items.answer: Relief of Lucknow
items.markingKey: (d) Relief of Lucknow: a painting by Thomas Jones Barker (1859) celebrating the British commanders who rescued the besieged British garrison at Lucknow.

items.stem: "The taluqdars of Awadh joined the revolt." Examine this statement with reference to Awadh in revolt.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The Summary Settlement of 1856 had taken away their estates, forts and power.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the Summary Settlement of 1856 had taken away their estates, forts and power.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: The taluqdars of Awadh joined the revolt.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The Summary Settlement of 1856 had taken away their estates, forts and power.
items.markingKey: (a) The Summary Settlement of 1856 had taken away their estates, forts and power.
options: The Summary Settlement of 1856 had taken away their estates, forts and power.
They came from Awadh's villages and their families suffered from high revenue demands and the loss of the Nawab.
It followed a similar pattern in different places and sepoys communicated through panchayats and messengers.
Taluqdars, peasants and sepoys all had grievances against the British and fought together.

items.stem: What is meant by 'sepoy' in the context of the pattern of the Revolt of 1857?
items.answer: An Indian soldier in the army of the East India Company.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sepoy correctly explained as an Indian soldier in the army of the East India Company.
